subject.title: [Bug]: Slack thread-session-key ACP binding routing test fails deterministically on main

question: Should the Slack configured ACP binding contract keep the test's expected route/request shape, or has the shared route object intentionally changed and the test should be updated?
rationale: The issue is protected by a maintainer label, and source inspection shows the failing assertion sits at the boundary between Slack prepare routing and shared configured-binding route resolution where either side could own the contract.

options.title: Fix routing to satisfy the existing contract
options.body: Treat the test as the intended behavior and repair Slack or shared route normalization so configured ACP bindings receive the expected request shape.

options.title: Update the test for the new route shape
options.body: If maintainers intended the shared route object change, update this Slack test to assert the new contract and add a short rationale near the assertion.

options.title: Defer to broader ACP thread-binding design
options.body: Only choose this if the failure is inseparable from the broader ACP thread-binding preset work tracked elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Fix routing to satisfy the existing contract
recommendation.body: Treat the test as the intended behavior and repair Slack or shared route normalization so configured ACP bindings receive the expected request shape.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the Slack configured ACP binding test, Slack routing, and shared binding-route surfaces.
